subject: POC: Acme Retail - Access provisioning & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: POC recap & next steps (access + success criteria)

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned for the POC:

Summary of goals (as discussed)
- Validate latency and cost at 1k QPS-equivalent workload for search reranking flows.
- Verify output quality (top-5 rerank precision) vs current model baseline.
- Confirm integration latency under realistic request sizes (avg 256 tokens).

Success criteria (proposed)
1) 95th percentile generation latency < 250ms for single-request rerank path under our dedicated POC config.
2) Top-5 precision >= current baseline + 6 percentage points on your labelled eval set.
3) Integration validated end-to-end in staging with API key + IP allowlist and SSO login for two engineers.

Timeline
- Week 1 (this week): access & credentials provisioned; initial smoke tests.
- Week 2: ingest eval set, run baseline and Redwood runs.
- Week 3: tune config / batching; measure cost metrics and collect results for a decision meeting.

Ownership
- Acme: Sara Thompson (product lead), Tom Garcia (platform/infra) — provide eval set & IP ranges, confirm SSO config.
- Redwood: Marissa (account lead) + Dylan (SE) — provision POC workspace, generate API keys, support eval runs, and collect metrics.

Access items we need from you to kick off
1) SAML SSO invite: please share the IdP metadata or add redwood-sso@redwood.com as a trusted SP.
2) IP allowlist: CIDR ranges you want us to lock POC API keys to.
3) A list of two user emails who should get SSO access (product + infra).
4) Temporary access window target: start next Monday (2026-02-23) for ~3 weeks.

Attachments: redwood-poc-guide.pdf (POC steps, what we monitor, template eval script).

If that all looks good I’ll get Dylan to provision the POC project and share credentials. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Mobile: (415) 555-0198

---
Redwood Inference — production LLM inference for engineering teams

From: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Garcia <tgarcia@acmeretail.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC recap & next steps (access + success criteria)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal notes. Confirming the success criteria and timeline look good to Acme. A couple of clarifications and the items we can provide: 

What we can provide now
- Eval set: we’ll drop a sanitized sample (10k rows) into the shared Drive by EOD Monday.
- IP allowlist: attaching a CSV of CIDR ranges used by our staging infra (acme-ip-allowlist.csv).
- SSO: we can add redwood-sso@acmeretail.com as an SP; I’ve looped Tom to share the IdP metadata.
- Users for SSO: sara.thompson@acmeretail.com, tgarcia@acmeretail.com

Timeline note: Our infra prefers the POC window to start 2026-02-24 so Tom can clear a maintenance window; end date is flexible, but goal is to have preliminary results by 2026-03-16 (open to compressing to 3 weeks if provisioning is fast).

Requests for Redwood
- We need a dedicated API key for the POC that can be IP-restricted, and a brief readme on how to rotate keys if needed.
- SSO test instructions (SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated flows) — our SAML admin will validate.
- Please share any rate limit or concurrency assumptions so we can provision client-side throttles.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Thompson
Product Lead, Search & Recommendations
Acme Retail
sara.thompson@acmeretail.com

Hi Dylan —

Forwarding Sara’s confirmation. Can you provision the POC workspace and create the following items?
- One API key scoped to the Acme POC project (label: ACME-POC-2026). Please enable IP allowlist enforcement.
- Generate a credentials stub file (poc-credentials-stub.txt) we can share with Acme once masked.
- Send SSO invite (SAML) to sara.thompson@acmeretail.com and tgarcia@acmeretail.com — they’ll validate IdP metadata.
- Share a short runbook for rotating keys and any rate-limit guidance we should pass to Acme.

Timeline: they prefer provisioning by 2026-02-24/25 so they can start testing week of 02/24.

Let me know if you need anything from me (service account, project id).

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Cc: Tom Garcia <tgarcia@acmeretail.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0800

Hi all —

Quick status update on provisioning:
- POC project created: redwood-acme-poc-2026
- API key created and labeled ACME-POC-2026; key id (masked) ri-poc-****-abcd. We have enabled IP allowlist per the attached ranges.
- SSO invites sent: sara.thompson@acmeretail.com, tgarcia@acmeretail.com — please check spam if you don't see them; the invite originates from redwood-sso@redwood.com.
- Attached: poc-credentials-stub.txt (contains connection endpoints, key id stub, and short rotation steps).
- Rate-limit guidance: start at 50rps with 4 concurrent connections and dial up while monitoring 95th-pct latency. Dylan is available to run initial smoke tests with you.

Next steps recommended
1) Acme: confirm you received SSO invites and can log in.
2) Acme: confirm IP allowlist is accepted and the staging CIDRs in acme-ip-allowlist.csv map to what we configured.
3) Redwood: we’ll run an initial 1000-sample eval with your sanitized set and share the first-pass latency/cost numbers by EOD 2026-03-04.

If you want, I can schedule a 30-min smoke test next Wed (03/04) to validate connectivity and run the evaluation harness.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
